description: The Mobility Database is an open catalogue of public transport and shared mobility data feeds: GTFS Schedule timetables, GTFS Realtime feeds and GBFS bike-share and scooter feeds. It is hosted and maintained by MobilityData, the non-profit organisation that stewards these standards, to give developers, operators, researchers and map applications one place to find current and historical feeds. The site states more than 6,000 feeds in over 99 countries; the catalogue CSV read on 2026-09-26 listed 6,475 GTFS and GTFS Realtime feeds in 95 countries, led by the United States, France, Japan and Canada. Coverage per feed is the operator's own network (stops, routes, trips, schedules, fares where published), so resolution is individual stops and departures. Access is through the web search, a catalogue CSV (feeds_v2.csv) with each feed's source URL, licence URL, bounding box and a mirrored latest copy, the catalogue repository on GitHub, and a REST API that needs a free sign-up. Feeds are checked daily and mirrored to avoid operator downtime and geoblocking. Metadata generated by MobilityData is CC0 1.0 and the API code Apache-2.0; the content of each feed stays under its owner's licence, which users must respect. Caveats: coverage is only what operators or contributors register, so many smaller or non-Western operators are missing, and feeds vary in quality (validator reports are attached). It is the main input for building transit networks for network flow, accessibility, agent-based and capacity planning models, and relates to the GTFS specification and to Transitland, a parallel feed registry.
